claims.text: The nanoparticles begin as disordered, near-equiatomic solid solutions with homogeneous elemental mixing.
High configurational entropy governs the structural and chemical stability of multi-element near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered solid-solution state rather than phase-separated or intermetallic states.
Severe lattice distortion causes sluggish atomic diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion inhibits elemental segregation and phase separation.
Nanoparticles with robust diffusion barriers undergo minimal phase evolution under service conditions.
In situ TEM or synchrotron X-ray diffraction will be used during controlled heating to monitor elemental distribution and crystal structure in real time.
The relevant operating ranges are 773–1173 K for catalysis and 473–1923 K for thermoelectric use.
Changes in atomic-scale elemental distributions and lattice distortions signal the onset of segregation or a phase transformation.
Relative to a diffusion-unimpeded baseline, entropy-stabilized nanoparticles will exhibit less elemental segregation during heating.
Relative to the baseline, entropy-stabilized nanoparticles will retain a disordered solid-solution structure during heating.
Samples lacking diffusion barriers or exposed to excessively high temperatures will show phase separation or ordered-phase formation.
Pre-annealing can relax lattice distortions and thereby promote diffusion.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will exhibit progressive elemental segregation and phase transitions under conditions where as-synthesized nanoparticles remain stable.
The proposed stabilization applies only within the specified temperature windows and finite exposure times.
At higher temperatures or after prolonged exposure, diffusion can overcome the kinetic barriers and produce segregation.
The influence of low noble-metal content on diffusion dynamics and kinetic barriers is not quantified and may vary.
Comparable segregation and phase-transition behavior in the as-synthesized and annealed sets would falsify the proposed entropy-plus-kinetic-barrier explanation.
